issue.title: Bug: test_gnoi_system_reboot_warm teardown fails on t0/vs after PR #23997 — gnmi_tls fixture rollback races with post-test YANG validation

failure.body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Medium

### Description of the bug

 ## Summary

Since `4f4cf8044a` (PR #23997, "Fix TLS authentication failure in test_gnoi_system_reboot", merged 2026-04-20 ~18:41
UTC), `gnmi/test_gnoi_system_reboot.py::test_gnoi_system_reboot_warm` consistently errors on **teardown** on
master/t0/vs. The test body itself passes; the failure is in the post-test YANG validation hook reporting `container ...
 is not running` and `Unable to connect to redis (unix-socket) – Cannot assign requested address`.

 ## Impact

 Module-level fail rate on master/t0/vs:

 | Date | Fail % |
 |---|---|
 | Apr 3 – Apr 19 | 0 % (>14 days clean, 3000+ runs) |
 | **Apr 20 (regression day)** | 4.3 % |
 | Apr 21 | 13.0 % |
 | Apr 22 | 14.6 % |
 | Apr 23 (partial) | 35.7 % |

 Affected scope (since Apr 20):

 | Topology | ASIC | Runs | Fails | Fail % |
 |---|---|---|---|---|
 | **t0** | vs | 250 | 58 | **23.2 %** |
 | t1-lag | vs | 197 | 1 | 0.5 % |
 | t1-8-lag | vs | 251 | 0 | 0 % |
 | t2 | vs | 238 | 0 | 0 % |

 Only `test_gnoi_system_reboot_warm` is affected; `test_gnoi_system_reboot_cold` continues to pass.

### Steps to Reproduce

 ## Reproduction

 Any PR pipeline that runs the `impacted-area-kvmtest-t0` job on master will hit it intermittently. Recent example
testplan:

https://elastictest.org/scheduler/testplan/69e96446678eea40b1d997fa?testcase=gnmi%2Ftest_gnoi_system_reboot.py%7C%7C%7C2&type=console

 (All three retry attempts `|||0`, `|||1`, `|||2` failed identically.)

 ## Failure signature (from test log)

 ```text
 test_gnoi_system_reboot.py::test_gnoi_system_reboot_cold PASSED     [ 50%]
 test_gnoi_system_reboot.py::test_gnoi_system_reboot_warm PASSED     [100%]
 test_gnoi_system_reboot.py::test_gnoi_system_reboot_warm ERROR      [100%]

 ERROR at teardown of test_gnoi_system_reboot_warm
 ERROR | YANG validation failed on vlab-01 (post-test):
        Error response from daemon: container 290cab99f3f1f66adb2f99e2bf386ff... is not running
        Error: Unable to connect to redis (unix-socket) - Connection refused(1): Cannot assign requested address
        Failed: post-test YANG validation failed

 not running in container 'swss' are: ['buffermgrd','fabricmgrd','fdbsyncd','intfmgrd','nbrmgrd',
                                       'neighsyncd','portmgrd','tunnelmgrd','vlanmgrd','vrfmgrd','vxlanmgrd']
 not running in container 'bgp'  are: ['bgpcfgd','bgpd','fpmsyncd','staticd','zebra']
 not running in container 'teamd' are: ['teamsyncd']
 not running in container 'dhcp_relay' are: ['dhcp-relay:dhcp6relayd','dhcp-relay:dhcprelayd']
 ```

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

 ## Root cause

 PR #23997 introduced a new `gnmi_tls` fixture in `tests/common/fixtures/grpc_fixtures.py`. Its `finally`-block teardown
 calls:

 ```python
 finally:
     logger.info("Cleaning up gNOI TLS server environment")
     try:
         output = rollback(duthost, checkpoint_name)
         ...
     except Exception as e:
         logger.error("Configuration rollback failed with exception: %s", e)
     # No wait_critical_processes / wait_for_startup before returning
 ```

 After `test_gnoi_system_reboot_warm` runs, the in-memory config has drifted from the pre-test checkpoint, so `rollback`
 triggers a real `config replace` → restarts `swss`, `bgp`, `teamd`, `dhcp_relay` containers. The fixture returns
immediately without waiting for those containers to come back. Pytest then runs the post-test YANG validation hook,
which `docker exec`s into those very containers mid-restart and fails.

 This explains:

 - **Why only WARM, not COLD**: cold reboot's checkpoint matches the post-startup state, so `rollback` is a no-op; warm
reboot leaves drift, so `rollback` does real work.
 - **Why mainly t0 and not t1/t2**: t0 has more dynamic services (DHCP relay, VLAN intfs, single host-facing DUT) ⇒
larger rollback diff ⇒ longer container restart window.
 - **Why same-image runs flip pass→fail across the same day**: same OS image (`SONiC.master.1093447-6c9e8c302`) passed
at 10:23 UTC and failed at 22:30 UTC on Apr 20; only sonic-mgmt master moved.

 ## Suggested fix

 In the `gnmi_tls` fixture cleanup (`tests/common/fixtures/grpc_fixtures.py`), wait for critical processes after
rollback:

 ```python
 finally:
     logger.info("Cleaning up gNOI TLS server environment")
     try:
         output = rollback(duthost, checkpoint_name)
         ...
     except Exception as e:
         logger.error("Configuration rollback failed with exception: %s", e)

     # Wait for containers to come back before returning to pytest
     from tests.common.platform.processes_utils import wait_critical_processes
     wait_critical_processes(duthost)
 ```

 ## Suspect commit

 `4f4cf8044a` — sonic-net/sonic-mgmt PR [#23997](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/pull/23997) "Fix TLS
authentication failure in test_gnoi_system_reboot" (author: @ravaliyel, merged 2026-04-20 18:41 UTC).

 ## Environment

 - Branch: master
 - Topology: t0 (KVM virtual, `vlab-01`)
 - ASIC: vs
 - Image: `SONiC.master.1093447-6c9e8c302` and later
 - sonic-mgmt: master at `4f4cf8044a` and later

resolution.title: Fix gnmi_tls fixture teardown race: wait for critical processes after config rollback
resolution.description:
After `test_gnoi_system_reboot_warm`, config drift causes `rollback()` in the `gnmi_tls` fixture teardown to trigger a real `config replace`, restarting containers (`swss`, `bgp`, `teamd`, `dhcp_relay`). The fixture returned immediately, so the post-test YANG validation hook ran `docker exec` into mid-restarting containers and failed.

## Changes

- **`tests/common/fixtures/grpc_fixtures.py`**: In the `gnmi_tls` fixture `finally` block, call `wait_critical_processes(duthost)` after `rollback()` to block until all critical processes are healthy before returning to pytest. Wrapped in `try/except` so a wait failure doesn't mask the original test result.

```python
finally:
    try:
        output = rollback(duthost, checkpoint_name)
        ...
    except Exception as e:
        logger.error("Configuration rollback failed with exception: %s", e)

    try:
        logger.info("Waiting for critical processes to be healthy after rollback")
        wait_critical_processes(duthost)
        logger.info("All critical processes are healthy")
    except Exception as e:
        logger.error("Waiting for critical processes failed with exception: %s", e)
```

Only `test_gnoi_system_reboot_warm` was affected (not `cold`) because cold reboot's checkpoint matches the post-startup state, making `rollback` a no-op. The race is more pronounced on `t0` due to more dynamic services (DHCP relay, VLAN interfaces).
